beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Better teaching pictures do more than decorate. These twenty-four isometric props make actions visible: selecting evidence, granting permission, handing off work, and recording decisions.

qc.sparse_reason: Show-tell: one large native-vector prop and two readable labels. Only underfill and clustering waived.

props.text:
Teaching pictures should
decorate the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A prop is a reusable drawing. A state tells us what condition it is in. An action changes that condition. The picture shows the change; the voice explains why it matters.

qc.sparse_reason: Show-tell: one large native-vector prop and two readable labels. Only underfill and clustering waived.

beats.narration_text: Start with a dataset. Lift one record out of the collection. The motion distinguishes the evidence we actually inspect from everything we could inspect.

beats.narration_text: Linked data adds a relationship. Join the connector to the records. A link tells us where material connects, not whether that material is reliable.

beats.narration_text: Layers separate responsibilities. Lift the top layer while the others stay put. Use this to distinguish the interface, the agent, and the underlying service.

beats.narration_text: A reference gives the worker a procedure when it is needed. Pull out the marked section. Keep instructions visually distinct from evidence about the world.

beats.narration_text: The terminal takes a request and returns a result. Watch the evidence slip enter, then a different slip emerge. An action has an observable consequence.

beats.narration_text: Connected services exchange something specific. Draw the connection, then send a packet across it. Do not use a cable to imply unlimited access.

beats.narration_text: Deployment moves a package into its operating position. Lower the code onto its platform. This shows delivery, not a guarantee that the software works correctly.

beats.narration_text: A network offers more than one route. Follow one packet through the nodes. Showing the chosen path is clearer than lighting up every connection at once.

beats.narration_text: The raised hand means stop and ask. Raise it before the action continues. Human intervention belongs inside the workflow, not in a disclaimer after it.

beats.narration_text: A reviewer inspects a proposed result before approving it. Bring the evidence to the person, then add the check. Approval is a decision, not decoration.

beats.narration_text: Agreement needs two sides. Bring the hands together only after both are present. Use this for accepted terms or a shared task boundary, not automatic trust.

shot.visual_intent: Two separated hands meet
shot.motion_claim: Two separated hands meet

beats.narration_text: A handoff transfers responsibility. Move the same evidence slip from one person to another. The object persists, so the viewer can follow what changed hands.

beats.narration_text: A policy is a constraint that changes behavior. Let a request approach the boundary and stop. If the rule never affects the action, the picture teaches nothing.

beats.narration_text: Permission is a gate. Keep the lock closed until access is granted, then open it. The shield represents this boundary, not proof that a system is secure.

beats.narration_text: Uncertainty should change the route. Send the unresolved case away for review. A question mark is useful only when the workflow does something about it.

beats.narration_text: Cross-check two records before adding either check mark. These symbols show the comparison step. They cannot tell us whether the underlying sources are independent or correct.

beats.narration_text: Inspection is an active search. Move the lens across the source, then mark the selected finding. Finding a passage and verifying its claim are different jobs.

beats.narration_text: Revision needs a before and an after. Separate the versions and reveal the changed line. Keep enough history to explain why the new version is better.

beats.narration_text: A process record accumulates as work happens. Add each row in order. Record the action, the evidence, and the decision, not just the finished artifact.

beats.narration_text: Delegation starts with a responsible owner. Draw the branches, then send work to each destination. Different workers need explicit tasks, not merely different boxes.

beats.narration_text: A decision changes the path. Split the moving token into two possible routes. In a real workflow, state the condition that selects one route rather than both.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Use Show-Tell to explain my workflow with three props. Show one human decision and one check of the evidence. Then check the film yourself. Does every motion explain a change? Can you tell what the human decided?
